I did not run `make check`, `make test` or pytest, as you instructed. The test counts come from `uv run --locked pytest --collect-only -q`. "Exit 0, ruff and mypy clean" comes from CI run 45408968632 (`151 passed in 11.94s`, `All checks passed!`, `no issues found`). I skipped `make load` because `scripts/load.py` is being edited. Its figures were checked against the notes. I ran the acceptance curls and the S2 loop live, then ran `make reset`. The database is back at 5000000/50000/200000 with 0 payments and 0 keys.

## Findings, most important first

1. `git clone https://github.com/yujinio/ta-firm-payments-challenge.git` … `make up` (README:29-31). **Missing or misleading.** `gh repo view` gives `defaultBranchRef: main`. `git ls-tree --name-only origin/main` lists only `.gitignore` and `docs`. A clean clone has no Makefile, so `make up` fails. The code is only on `feat/bulk-payment-service`, and no PR is open. Fix: merge to `main` before sending the link, or use `git clone -b feat/bulk-payment-service`.

2. "`ai-logs/` holds every working session: the design sessions, the controller session with every subagent's transcript, and the review session" (README:432). **Wrong** for the repository as it stands. `find ai-logs` shows only `ai-logs/.gitkeep` (0 B). Task §3 and §7.2 require unedited logs. As a result, every claim in README:409-454 about models, reviews and rulings can't be checked. Also, plan.md:48 says "the independent review (Task 9, Step 1) is still to run", so no review session exists yet, and Step 5 (agent-workflow.md:35) is missing from the README:411-421 table. Fix: commit the logs. Either list the review session once it has run, or drop it.

3. The two-question checklists at README:477-488 are all unchecked. **Missing.** assignment.md:158 says "At the end of the README, also answer two quick questions". Fix: the author ticks one box in each, and fills in the hours if it's more than 6h.

4. "Several started as the model's proposals that I accepted. These include `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, `JSON` instead of `JSONB`, storing only successful responses … They are marked **[P]**" (README:446). **Wrong.**
   - spec.md:103 marks "Only the successful 201 response" **[R]**. README:442 also lists it under [R], so the README contradicts itself.
   - `grep -n "\[P\]" docs/spec.md` finds no marker on `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (spec.md:389) or on JSON/JSONB (spec.md:254).
   - spec.md:11 defines [P] as "proposal … not yet confirmed separately", not "accepted".
   - Fix: list only the items that really are [P]: the single error format (spec.md:338) and the key format (spec.md:282). Restate [P] the way the spec defines it.

5. "Every AI-written commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer that names its model" (README:430), together with "Design and specification | Claude Fable 5.2" (README:413-414). **Wrong.** Commit fce9a5b ("docs: design spec, implementation plan and agent workflow") carries `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`, and no commit names Fable 5.2. Fix: say the trailer names the model of the session that made the commit, and that the Opus session committed the Fable-authored spec and plan. Or correct the trailer.

6. "I used **Claude Code** with three Claude models" plus "Sonnet 5.5 and once Haiku 5.5 for small re-reviews" (README:409, 419). **Wrong / Unsupported.** The README contradicts itself: that's four models. Haiku appears nowhere in agent-workflow.md or plan.md:90-97. Task reviewers' models aren't recorded; only the 4b re-reviewer (Sonnet) is, at agent-workflow.md:34. Fix: "four models", and back the reviewer split with the logs, or drop it.

7. Process counts with no source: "Three important findings, fixed in one wave" (README:420), "Two aborted early attempts" (README:435), "about twenty rulings" (README:448). **Unsupported.**
   - plan.md:45 lists four fix-wave items: the Content-Type message; host ports with loopback; body limit with Host forwarding; the CI `stand` job.
   - agent-workflow.md:18 gives no count of aborted attempts.
   - Fix: match the counts to the logs once they are committed, or drop the numbers.

8. Decision ownership contradicts itself.
   - "I kept the limit at 1,000" (README:331) versus "the controller model made … rulings on its own … keeping the 1,000 limit" (README:451). **Wrong.**
   - "So I broke the service three ways" (README:157) versus README:418, where the Opus subagents ran the mutation check (plan Task 7). **Wrong.**
   - "`make load` not resetting the database by itself" as a controller ruling (README:454). **Unsupported.** plan.md:46 calls the host-uv move of `make load` "the author's decision", and no doc records the no-reset ruling.
   - Fix: pick one owner for each decision and match it to the logs.

9. "My first draft of the mutation check was wrong. In the final check, removing `ORDER BY` (M2) is a mutation the tests do catch, through C3" (README:357), filed under "During design (found by throwaway probes…)". **Wrong.**
   - The first notes version (`git show 95e72a0:docs/verification-notes.md`) already had C3 catching M2.
   - What was wrong was the stated cause: "LockRows over Seq Scan". 7c7f885 replaced it once auto_explain showed a Bitmap Heap Scan.
   - That happened during implementation, not in the design probes. The PG 19 and "Docker was not available" bullets (README:355-356) aren't probe findings either.
   - Fix: "My first write-up gave an unverified cause for C2 staying green under M2; the plan was a Bitmap Heap Scan, and the cause is now left open." Move it to "During implementation".

10. "To stop the stand, run `docker compose down`. To drop the data as well, run `docker compose down -v`" (README:83). **Misleading.** docker-compose.yml declares no named volume. `docker inspect` on db-1 shows an anonymous `volume 2fa7c8fd… -> /var/lib/postgresql`. After `down`, the next `make up` creates a new container with a fresh volume, so the firms are gone and `make seed` is needed. `-v` only removes the orphaned volume. Fix: "`docker compose stop` keeps the data; `docker compose down -v` removes everything; after `down`, run `make up` and `make seed` again." Alternatively, add a named volume.

11. Test descriptions that overstate the tests:
    - "I5 | 8 simultaneous requests with one key: one execution, 7 byte-identical replays" (README:153). **Wrong.** test_races.py:140 compares parsed dicts (`body == bodies[0]`). Bytes are compared in C7: test_multiprocess.py:157 `r.content == responses[0].content`. Fix: "7 identical replays (byte-identical over HTTP in C7)".
    - "`tests/api` | 63 | … I1–I9 cover idempotency" (README:138). **Wrong.** I5 is `tests/concurrency/test_races.py::test_i5_same_key_in_parallel`. Fix: "I1–I4, I6–I9".
    - "C1 | … exactly three 201s, seven 422s" (README:145). C1 runs in-process and counts `created`/`insufficient_funds` (test_races.py:54). The HTTP statuses come from C7 (test_multiprocess.py:138). Fix: "three accepted, seven `insufficient_funds`".

12. "The largest valid request is 1,000 payments with 500-character non-ASCII descriptions, about 1.1 MB" (README:317). **Wrong** arithmetic. spec.md:150 repeats the figure. 1.1 MB holds only for 2-byte characters. With json.dumps, 1,000 × 500 3-byte characters is 1.60 MB, 4-byte emoji is 2.10 MB, and emoji as `\uXXXX` escapes is 6.10 MB. The length check is Python `len()` (service.py:87). JSON whitespace makes the true maximum unbounded. All of these still fit under 8 MB. Fix: "a 1,000-payment batch with 500-character descriptions is 1.1 to 6.1 MB depending on encoding".

13. "the median is 196 ms and the maximum 257.6 ms" (README:331) versus the Load table, max-batch p50 "193.2" (README:183). **Misleading:** the same run shows two medians with no explanation. verification-notes.md:319-321 explains that `statistics.median` gives 196.0 and nearest-rank gives 193.2. Fix: use 193.2 (p50), or add the half-sentence from the notes.

14. Claims whose only possible source is the missing logs. **Unsupported.**
    - "nginx still pointed at the old addresses and returned 504" (README:367). No doc mentions a 504 from the stale balancer. plan.md:43 records only the restart.
    - "A JSON escape such as `"\ud800"` … caused a 500" (README:364). No doc or commit message records the 500. Tests and comments (schemas.py:44) show only that it is rejected now.
    - "publish a retention period of at least 24 hours" (README:393). spec.md:654 says only "a time-to-live and periodic cleanup".
    - "`docs/verification-notes.md` records every measured and observed result quoted below" (README:5). The probe figures (2,400/80, 109 ms per 1,000 payments, the 40-thread default) are in spec §5.7 and §17. Fix: "the notes and spec section 17".

15. "Docker with Compose v2: Docker Desktop, Docker Engine, or Podman with `docker-compose`" (README:22). **Misleading.** The Makefile calls `docker compose`. The verified local setup is a `docker` shim to Podman (`docker --version` gives `podman version 5.8.2`), rootful (`podman machine inspect` gives `true`), with Docker Compose v5.1.3 as provider (spec.md:596). README:401 meanwhile warns that legacy `docker-compose` v1 ignores `deploy.replicas`. Fix: "Podman with a `docker` command (podman-docker) and Docker Compose v2+ as the compose provider; verified rootful".

16. "The same key with a different body gives `422 idempotency_key_reuse`" (README:118), plus the S3 row (README:194). **Missing:** no command is given for either, and spec.md:632 step 9 expects reviewers to run S3. Fix: add a curl with `-H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-1' --data-binary @format-example-request.json`. I ran it: 422 `idempotency_key_reuse`. Also add the S3 commands (`docker stop $(docker compose ps -q app | head -1)`, five posts with one key, then `make up`).

## Verified correct
- Test counts, with collect-only and CI both giving 151 = 64 unit / 6 db / 63 api / 18 concurrency, and the test names in the tables.
- Live: sample → 201 with the exact README body (ids 1-3, total "13251.25"). Balances 3674875 / 170075 / 1405050. The three repeats gave 201, 201, 422 with the exact insufficient_funds JSON.

- Transaction order: `set_config('lock_timeout','5000ms',true)`, then key claim, then one `IN (...) ORDER BY id` with `with_for_update(key_share=True)` (FOR NO KEY UPDATE), then checks, insert, update, store response (service.py:179-248).

A clean clone has no Makefile, so `make up` fails. The code is only on `feat/bulk-payment-service`, and no PR is open. Fix: merge to `main` before sending the link, or use `git clone -b feat/bulk-payment-service`.

2. "`ai-logs/` holds every working session: the design sessions, the controller session with every subagent's transcript, and the review session" (README:432). **Wrong** for the repository as it stands. `find ai-logs` shows only `ai-logs/.gitkeep` (0 B). Task §3 and §7.2 require unedited logs. As a result, every claim in README:409-454 about models, reviews and rulings can't be checked. Also, plan.md:48 says "the independent review (Task 9, Step 1) is still to run", so no review session exists yet, and Step 5 (agent-workflow.md:35) is missing from the README:411-421 table. Fix: commit the logs. Either list the review session once it has run, or drop it.

3. The two-question checklists at README:477-488 are all unchecked. **Missing.** assignment.md:158 says "At the end of the README, also answer two quick questions". Fix: the author ticks one box in each, and fills in the hours if it's more than 6h.

4. "Several started as the model's proposals that I accepted. These include `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, `JSON` instead of `JSONB`, storing only successful responses … They are marked **[P]**" (README:446). **Wrong.**
   - spec.md:103 marks "Only the successful 201 response" **[R]**. README:442 also lists it under [R], so the README contradicts itself.
   - `grep -n "\[P\]" docs/spec.md` finds no marker on `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (spec.md:389) or on JSON/JSONB (spec.md:254).
   - spec.md:11 defines [P] as "proposal … not yet confirmed separately", not "accepted".
   - Fix: list only the items that really are [P]: the single error format (spec.md:338) and the key format (spec.md:282). Restate [P] the way the spec defines it.

5. "Every AI-written commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer that names its model" (README:430), together with "Design and specification | Claude Fable 5.2" (README:413-414). **Wrong.** Commit fce9a5b ("docs: design spec, implementation plan and agent workflow") carries `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`, and no commit names Fable 5.2. Fix: say the trailer names the model of the session that made the commit, and that the Opus session committed the Fable-authored spec and plan. Or correct the trailer.

6. "I used **Claude Code** with three Claude models" plus "Sonnet 5.5 and once Haiku 5.5 for small re-reviews" (README:409, 419). **Wrong / Unsupported.** The README contradicts itself: that's four models. Haiku appears nowhere in agent-workflow.md or plan.md:90-97. Task reviewers' models aren't recorded; only the 4b re-reviewer (Sonnet) is, at agent-workflow.md:34. Fix: "four models", and back the reviewer split with the logs, or drop it.

7. Process counts with no source: "Three important findings, fixed in one wave" (README:420), "Two aborted early attempts" (README:435), "about twenty rulings" (README:448). **Unsupported.**
   - plan.md:45 lists four fix-wave items: the Content-Type message; host ports with loopback; body limit with Host forwarding; the CI `stand` job.
   - agent-workflow.md:18 gives no count of aborted attempts.
   - Fix: match the counts to the logs once they are committed, or drop the numbers.

8. Decision ownership contradicts itself.
   - "I kept the limit at 1,000" (README:331) versus "the controller model made … rulings on its own … keeping the 1,000 limit" (README:451). **Wrong.**
   - "So I broke the service three ways" (README:157) versus README:418, where the Opus subagents ran the mutation check (plan Task 7). **Wrong.**
   - "`make load` not resetting the database by itself" as a controller ruling (README:454). **Unsupported.** plan.md:46 calls the host-uv move of `make load` "the author's decision", and no doc records the no-reset ruling.
   - Fix: pick one owner for each decision and match it to the logs.

9. "My first draft of the mutation check was wrong. In the final check, removing `ORDER BY` (M2) is a mutation the tests do catch, through C3" (README:357), filed under "During design (found by throwaway probes…)". **Wrong.**
   - The first notes version (`git show 95e72a0:docs/verification-notes.md`) already had C3 catching M2.
   - What was wrong was the stated cause: "LockRows over Seq Scan". 7c7f885 replaced it once auto_explain showed a Bitmap Heap Scan.
   - That happened during implementation, not in the design probes. The PG 19 and "Docker was not available" bullets (README:355-356) aren't probe findings either.
   - Fix: "My first write-up gave an unverified cause for C2 staying green under M2; the plan was a Bitmap Heap Scan, and the cause is now left open." Move it to "During implementation".

10. "To stop the stand, run `docker compose down`. To drop the data as well, run `docker compose down -v`" (README:83). **Misleading.** docker-compose.yml declares no named volume. `docker inspect` on db-1 shows an anonymous `volume 2fa7c8fd… -> /var/lib/postgresql`. After `down`, the next `make up` creates a new container with a fresh volume, so the firms are gone and `make seed` is needed. `-v` only removes the orphaned volume. Fix: "`docker compose stop` keeps the data; `docker compose down -v` removes everything; after `down`, run `make up` and `make seed` again." Alternatively, add a named volume.

11. Test descriptions that overstate the tests:
    - "I5 | 8 simultaneous requests with one key: one execution, 7 byte-identical replays" (README:153). **Wrong.** test_races.py:140 compares parsed dicts (`body == bodies[0]`). Bytes are compared in C7: test_multiprocess.py:157 `r.content == responses[0].content`. Fix: "7 identical replays (byte-identical over HTTP in C7)".
    - "`tests/api` | 63 | … I1–I9 cover idempotency" (README:138). **Wrong.** I5 is `tests/concurrency/test_races.py::test_i5_same_key_in_parallel`. Fix: "I1–I4, I6–I9".
    - "C1 | … exactly three 201s, seven 422s" (README:145). C1 runs in-process and counts `created`/`insufficient_funds` (test_races.py:54). The HTTP statuses come from C7 (test_multiprocess.py:138). Fix: "three accepted, seven `insufficient_funds`".

12. "The largest valid request is 1,000 payments with 500-character non-ASCII descriptions, about 1.1 MB" (README:317). **Wrong** arithmetic. spec.md:150 repeats the figure. 1.1 MB holds only for 2-byte characters. With json.dumps, 1,000 × 500 3-byte characters is 1.60 MB, 4-byte emoji is 2.10 MB, and emoji as `\uXXXX` escapes is 6.10 MB. The length check is Python `len()` (service.py:87). JSON whitespace makes the true maximum unbounded. All of these still fit under 8 MB. Fix: "a 1,000-payment batch with 500-character descriptions is 1.1 to 6.1 MB depending on encoding".

13. "the median is 196 ms and the maximum 257.6 ms" (README:331) versus the Load table, max-batch p50 "193.2" (README:183). **Misleading:** the same run shows two medians with no explanation. verification-notes.md:319-321 explains that `statistics.median` gives 196.0 and nearest-rank gives 193.2. Fix: use 193.2 (p50), or add the half-sentence from the notes.

14. Claims whose only possible source is the missing logs. **Unsupported.**
    - "nginx still pointed at the old addresses and returned 504" (README:367). No doc mentions a 504 from the stale balancer. plan.md:43 records only the restart.
    - "A JSON escape such as `"\ud800"` … caused a 500" (README:364). No doc or commit message records the 500. Tests and comments (schemas.py:44) show only that it is rejected now.
    - "publish a retention period of at least 24 hours" (README:393). spec.md:654 says only "a time-to-live and periodic cleanup".
    - "`docs/verification-notes.md` records every measured and observed result quoted below" (README:5). The probe figures (2,400/80, 109 ms per 1,000 payments, the 40-thread default) are in spec §5.7 and §17. Fix: "the notes and spec section 17".

15. "Docker with Compose v2: Docker Desktop, Docker Engine, or Podman with `docker-compose`" (README:22). **Misleading.** The Makefile calls `docker compose`. The verified local setup is a `docker` shim to Podman (`docker --version` gives `podman version 5.8.2`), rootful (`podman machine inspect` gives `true`), with Docker Compose v5.1.3 as provider (spec.md:596). README:401 meanwhile warns that legacy `docker-compose` v1 ignores `deploy.replicas`. Fix: "Podman with a `docker` command (podman-docker) and Docker Compose v2+ as the compose provider; verified rootful".

16. "The same key with a different body gives `422 idempotency_key_reuse`" (README:118), plus the S3 row (README:194). **Missing:** no command is given for either, and spec.md:632 step 9 expects reviewers to run S3. Fix: add a curl with `-H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-1' --data-binary @format-example-request.json`. I ran it: 422 `idempotency_key_reuse`. Also add the S3 commands (`docker stop $(docker compose ps -q app | head -1)`, five posts with one key, then `make up`).

## Verified correct
- Test counts, with collect-only and CI both giving 151 = 64 unit / 6 db / 63 api / 18 concurrency, and the test names in the tables.
- Live: sample → 201 with the exact README body (ids 1-3, total "13251.25"). Balances 3674875 / 170075 / 1405050. The three repeats gave 201, 201, 422 with the exact insufficient_funds JSON.
- Live: `curl -d` with no Content-Type → 422 with the exact `Content-Type: application/json` message.
- Live: `make reset` plus format-example → 201 with 4849925 / 170075 / 230000. The arithmetic 50,000 − 3 × 13,251.25 = 10,246.25 checks out.
- Live: `demo-1` twice → both 201, bodies byte-identical (`cmp`), `idempotent-replayed: true`, another upstream, 3 payments and 1 key.
- Live: the S2 loop → three X-Upstream lines (11/10/9).
- Page 3 is format-example and page 4 is the sample (pypdf on `docs/TA Firm Payments.pdf`).
- Make targets up, seed, reset, test, check and load match the Makefile. LB_PORT and DB_PORT apply in compose, the Makefile and conftest.
- Error codes, statuses, messages, `Retry-After: 1`, the 404/405/`http_error` mapping, and details limited to loc/msg/type (main.py, errors.py, service.py).
- Transaction order: `set_config('lock_timeout','5000ms',true)`, then key claim, then one `IN (...) ORDER BY id` with `with_for_update(key_share=True)` (FOR NO KEY UPDATE), then checks, insert, update, store response (service.py:179-248).
- 55P03/40P01 → busy with an ERROR log for deadlocks; pool `TimeoutError` → busy (service.py:160-171).
- Amount rules: `[0-9]` fullmatch, 11 characters, greater than 0, at most INT32_MAX, StrictStr; U+0000 and lone surrogates rejected (schemas.py). No float in app/.
- Key format 0x21-0x7E, 1-255 characters; first header wins; INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; SHA-256 over cents; JSON column, not JSONB; only 201 stored; per-payer scope (idempotency.py, migration 0001).
- Pool size 10, max_overflow=0, pool_pre_ping, hide_parameters; AnyIO limit set to 10 in lifespan; engine built once under a lock (db.py, main.py:74-76).
- Log record fields: request id from X-Request-Id, hostname, payer, count, total, outcome, duration (main.py:96-106).
- Compose: db on postgres:18, a one-shot migrate, 3 app replicas, nginx; ports bound to 127.0.0.1; `client_max_body_size 8m`; `proxy_connect_timeout 2s`; X-Upstream header.
- Concurrency details: Barrier, pg_stat_activity polling, I-1/I-2 per round, C2 20×50, C3 200 batches / 16 threads / seed 20261121, C7 `--workers 4`.
- Mutation table M1-M3, the 3-of-3 M2 deadlock result and the C2-clean observation (verification-notes:30-145).
- Load table, machine and VM specs, in-container client, the 1,100 firms with ids from 1000, script checks and exit code, the 619 batches/s figure (verification-notes:217-310, load.py).
- 50.3/69.9 ms uncontended, 196/257.6 ms contended, the 250 ms budget, and the probe table 109/206/1,067 (spec §5.7, notes:314-343).
- S1-S3 on Podman 5.8.2 with Compose v5.1.3; the 2 s connect timeout; the CI jobs `check` and `stand` (push and PR) on ubuntu-latest; run 45408968632 green.
- Probe facts: SET LOCAL syntax error, JSONB reordering, the pool error not being a DBAPIError, U+0000, PG 19 released 2026-11-19, 2,400/80 on PG 16 (spec §17).
- Assumptions 1-11 match spec §4. Limitations 1-14 match spec §15 and §9.3, apart from finding 14.

diff --git a/docs/spec.md b/docs/spec.md
index 7650608..7cab6e9 100644
--- a/docs/spec.md
+++ b/docs/spec.md
@@ -85,7 +85,7 @@ The service runs as several instances behind a load balancer and uses a relation
 | **Additive extension** | Optional `Idempotency-Key` header and a service table; the given tables and examples work unchanged | **[R] Chosen** |
 | Changing the given tables | `BIGINT`, `batch_id`, `created_at`, `CHECK` | Rejected: changes the columns and types the task gives for `firms` and `payments` |
 
-Rationale [R]: the task does not forbid extension, and without a key duplicates cannot be prevented. The task describes the platform's database as two tables; the chosen option keeps both exactly as given and adds a service table, `idempotency_keys`, next to them. The service writes to it only when a request carries the `Idempotency-Key` header, so a request made strictly as the task describes touches only the two given tables.
+Rationale [R]: the purpose of the extension is to exclude duplicate operations. A client that loses the response after a commit, to a timeout, a dropped connection or a crash, cannot tell whether its payments went through, and a plain retry creates a second batch. The server cannot tell a retry from a legitimate second batch (assumption 6), so only a key sent by the client can prevent the duplicate. This is a feature beyond what the task asks for: the task does not forbid extension, and without a key duplicates cannot be prevented. The task describes the platform's database as two tables; the chosen option keeps both exactly as given and adds a service table, `idempotency_keys`, next to them. The service writes to it only when a request carries the `Idempotency-Key` header, so a request made strictly as the task describes touches only the two given tables.
 
 ### 5.2. Where to store the idempotency key
 
@@ -146,6 +146,7 @@ The number is a property of the stand, not a capacity recommendation.
 **Consequences of the stand:**
 
 - Migrations run once, in a separate `migrate` service that the replicas wait for. Three replicas each running `alembic upgrade head` at start would race.
+- Before serving, each replica checks that the revision in `alembic_version` equals the head revision of the migrations in its image, and refuses to start if they differ. A replica never serves against a schema it was not built for, for example after a failed migration or when a newer image meets an older database.
 - Each replica is a single Uvicorn process. Replicas publish no host port. The balancer publishes `127.0.0.1:${LB_PORT:-8000}`; `db` publishes `127.0.0.1:${DB_PORT:-5432}` so that tests and the multi-process test server can run on the host. 1:# Firm Payments: a bulk payment service
2:
3:A web service with one endpoint, `POST /bulk-payments`. A firm sends a batch of payments to other firms. If the payer's balance covers the whole batch, the service does everything in one PostgreSQL transaction and answers **201**: it inserts the payments, debits the payer and credits every payee. If the balance does not cover the batch, nothing changes and the service answers **422**.
4:
5:The service runs as three replicas behind an nginx load balancer. Correctness across replicas comes from row locks in the database, not from anything held in a process. The implementation follows `docs/spec.md`, which records each design decision with the alternatives that were rejected. `docs/verification-notes.md` records every measured and observed result quoted below.
6:
7:- [Run it](#run-it)
8:- [Verify it](#verify-it)
9:- [API](#api)
10:- [Solution and approach](#solution-and-approach)
11:- [Issues I ran into](#issues-i-ran-into)
12:- [Assumptions](#assumptions)
13:- [Known limitations and possible improvements](#known-limitations-and-possible-improvements)
14:- [How I worked](#how-i-worked)
15:- [Repository layout](#repository-layout)
16:- [Two questions](#two-questions)
17:
18:## Run it
19:
20:**Prerequisites:**
21:
22:- Docker with Compose v2: Docker Desktop, Docker Engine, or Podman with `docker-compose`.
23:- `make`.
24:- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), needed only for the tests and the load script. uv installs Python 3.14 itself if it is missing.
25:
26:The balancer listens on `127.0.0.1:8000` and the database on `127.0.0.1:5432`. If either port is taken, export `LB_PORT` and/or `DB_PORT` with other values before running the commands, and use your port in the URLs below.
27:
28:```bash
29:git clone https://github.com/yujinio/ta-firm-payments-challenge.git
30:cd ta-firm-payments-challenge
64:
65:These are $36,748.75, $1,700.75 and $14,050.50, as the task expects.
66:
67:Send `Content-Type: application/json` with every request. Without it, `curl -d` sends the body as a form, and the service answers 422 with the message `the request body must be JSON sent with Content-Type: application/json`.
68:
69:**Make targets** and what they run, if you prefer to run the commands yourself:
70:
71:| Target | Command |
72:|---|---|
73:| `make up` | `docker compose up --build -d --wait`, then `docker compose restart lb` |
74:| `make seed` | `docker compose exec -T db psql -U postgres -d firm_payments < scripts/seed.sql` |
75:| `make reset` | Truncates `payments`, `idempotency_keys` and `firms`, then runs the seed again |
76:| `make test` | `docker compose up -d --wait db`, then `uv run --locked pytest` |
77:| `make lint` | `uv run --locked ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy app scripts migrations` |
78:| `make check` | `make test` and `make lint` |
79:| `make load` | `uv run --locked python scripts/load.py --base-url http://localhost:8000 ...` (see [Load](#load)) |
80:
81:Use `make up`, not a bare `docker compose up`, whenever you bring the stand up again. nginx resolves the replica addresses only when it starts. Recreated replicas get new addresses, and `make up` restarts the balancer after them.
82:
83:To stop the stand, run `docker compose down`. To drop the data as well, run `docker compose down -v`.
84:
85:## Verify it
86:
87:### Acceptance walk-through
88:
89:This continues from [Run it](#run-it).
90:
91:1. Send the same sample request three more times. Expected: `201`, `201`, then `422`. After three batches Pinecrest has 50,000.00 − 3 × 13,251.25 = 10,246.25, which is less than one batch:
92:
93:   ```
94:   {"error":{"code":"insufficient_funds","message":"the payer's balance does not cover the batch total"}}
95:   ```
96:
97:2. Run `make reset` to return to the three seeded firms. Then send the request from page 3 of the task:
98:
99:   ```bash
100:   curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8000/bulk-payments \
125:   done | sort | uniq -c
126:   ```
127:
128:5. Run `make check`. Expected: exit code 0, with 151 tests passing and ruff and mypy clean.
129:
130:### Tests
131:
132:The tests run against a real PostgreSQL in the stand's `db` container, in a separate database called `firm_payments_test`. SQLite is never used, because lock behaviour is the thing under test. The schema comes from `alembic upgrade head`, and every test starts from the three seeded firms.
133:
134:| Group | Tests | What they show |
135:|---|---|---|
136:| `tests/unit` | 64 | Amount parsing (U1–U3): no float, full match of `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?`, the 32-bit bound. Also the request hash, the request schema, the command builder, and engine construction. |
137:| `tests/db` | 6 | Migrations apply to an empty database and roll back. The schema matches the spec. Payment descriptions never reach error logs. |
138:| `tests/api` | 63 | The HTTP contract. A1–A16 cover both samples from the task, every rejection code, the error format and the payment order. I1–I9 cover idempotency. |
139:| `tests/concurrency` | 18 | Races and locks; listed below. |
140:
141:The concurrency tests do not rely on lucky thread scheduling. Threads start together through a `threading.Barrier`, the race scenarios run for many rounds, and invariants I-1 (no negative balance) and I-2 (the sum of balances is unchanged) are checked after each round. Waits are detected by polling `pg_stat_activity`, not by sleeping.
142:
143:| Test | Scenario |
144:|---|---|
145:| C1 | 10 batches from one payer in parallel. The balance covers 3 of them: exactly three 201s, seven 422s. |
146:| C2 | 20 rounds of 50 crossing payments, A→B and B→A: no deadlock, no 503. |
147:| C3 | A cycle A→B→C→A plus a random mix: 200 batches on 16 threads with a fixed seed. |
148:| C4 | An external connection holds a firm's row lock. The request waits, then sees the committed balance. |
149:| C5, C8 | A lock or a key row is held longer than `lock_timeout`: 503 `busy`, nothing changed. |
150:| C6 | Many payers, one payee: the payee's balance equals the start plus all credits. |
151:| C7 | C1, I5 and crossing payments over HTTP against `uvicorn --workers 4`: separate processes that share only the database. |
152:| C9 | No free pool connection: 503 `busy`. |
153:| I5 | 8 simultaneous requests with one key: one execution, 7 byte-identical replays. |
154:
155:A statement-order test pins the SQL statements of spec section 8.2, in order.
156:
157:**Mutation check.** A concurrency test that stays green when the lock is removed proves nothing. So I broke the service three ways, one at a time, and ran the concurrency tests against each version:
158:
159:| Mutation | Behavioural tests that failed |
160:|---|---|
161:| M1: no `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` | C1, C2, C3, C4, C6 (too many batches accepted, lost updates, the sum of balances changed, a stale balance read) |
162:| M2: no `ORDER BY id` | C3, with real deadlocks, in 3 of 3 runs |
163:| M3: payer and payees locked in two queries | C2 and C3, with deadlocks |
164:
165:Details and log excerpts are in `docs/verification-notes.md`.
166:
167:### Static checks
168:
169:`make lint` runs three checks:
170:
185:
186:Measured on 2026-11-24 on an Apple M4 Pro, with the stand in a Podman VM (6 CPUs, 3.7 GiB). The client ran inside the Compose network, so the figures do not include the host-to-VM port forwarding that `make load` now goes through.
187:
188:| Scenario | Requests / concurrency | Requests/s | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | Statuses |
189:|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
190:| uniform | 2000 / 32 | 1036.5 | 30.5 | 54.3 | 62.7 | 201 × 2000 |
191:| hot-payer (one payer) | 2000 / 32 | 619.0 | 37.0 | 123.0 | 159.9 | 201 × 2000 |
192:| hot-payee (one payee) | 2000 / 32 | 627.4 | 35.0 | 123.5 | 157.8 | 201 × 2000 |
193:| max-batch (1,000 payments, one payer) | 40 / 4 | 19.5 | 193.2 | 239.4 | 257.6 | 201 × 40 |
194:| max-batch, no contention | 40 / 1 | 18.1 | 50.2 | 69.6 | 69.9 | 201 × 40 |
195:
196:In every run all invariant checks passed, there were no 503 or 500 responses, and requests split evenly over the three replicas. One payer sustained about 600 batches per second.
197:
198:### The stand
199:
200:| Check | Result |
201:|---|---|
202:| S1: `docker compose up -d --wait`, then `ps -a` | `db` and `lb` running, three `app` replicas healthy, `migrate` exited 0 |
203:| S2: 30 health checks through the balancer | Three distinct `X-Upstream` values |
204:| S3: stop one replica, then send the sample five times with one key | Five 201s, four of them replays. Balances changed once. |
205:
206:**Where it was verified:**
207:
208:- Locally, S1–S3 ran on Podman 5.8.2 with Docker Compose v5.1.3; no workaround was needed.
209:- On Docker Engine, the CI job `stand` runs `make up`, then `make seed`, posts the sample (201, Pinecrest 3674875) and checks for three upstreams. It runs on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runners on every push.
210:- The CI job `check` runs `make check`.
211:
212:## API
213:
214:```
215:POST /bulk-payments
216:Content-Type: application/json
217:Idempotency-Key: <optional, 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters>
218:```
219:
220:The body is exactly as in the task: `payer_firm_uuid` plus a list of `payments` with `amount`, `payee_firm_uuid` and `description`. The task leaves the path open; `/bulk-payments` is my choice.
221:
222:The 201 body echoes the payments in request order, with their new ids and normalised amounts. It does not include balances, because the request is not authenticated. `GET /healthz` checks the database connection.
223:
224:All errors share one format: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`. Validation errors add `details` (`loc`, `msg`, `type`), which never echo the rejected value. The task asks for 422 when a request is denied and does not distinguish reasons. So every rejection caused by the request is a 422, and `code` says why:
225:
226:| Status | `code` | When |
227:|---|---|---|
228:| 422 | `validation_error` | The body is not a JSON object, or a field breaks a rule: amount format, UUIDs, a missing `description`, an unknown field, more than 1,000 payments, a description longer than 500 characters, the key format |
229:| 422 | `self_payment` | A payment from the payer to itself |
230:| 422 | `firm_not_found` | The payer or a payee does not exist |
231:| 422 | `insufficient_funds` | The payer's balance does not cover the batch total |
232:| 422 | `balance_overflow` | A payee's balance would exceed 2,147,483,647 cents |
233:| 422 | `idempotency_key_reuse` | A key already used with a different request |
234:| 503 | `busy` | A lock wait or a pool wait timed out; `Retry-After: 1` |
235:| 500 | `internal_error` | Anything unexpected; details only in the logs |
236:| 404, 405, other | `not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, `http_error` | Routing errors, in the same format |

226:| Status | `code` | When |
227:|---|---|---|
228:| 422 | `validation_error` | The body is not a JSON object, or a field breaks a rule: amount format, UUIDs, a missing `description`, an unknown field, more than 1,000 payments, a description longer than 500 characters, the key format |
229:| 422 | `self_payment` | A payment from the payer to itself |
230:| 422 | `firm_not_found` | The payer or a payee does not exist |
231:| 422 | `insufficient_funds` | The payer's balance does not cover the batch total |
232:| 422 | `balance_overflow` | A payee's balance would exceed 2,147,483,647 cents |
233:| 422 | `idempotency_key_reuse` | A key already used with a different request |
234:| 503 | `busy` | A lock wait or a pool wait timed out; `Retry-After: 1` |
235:| 500 | `internal_error` | Anything unexpected; details only in the logs |
236:| 404, 405, other | `not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, `http_error` | Routing errors, in the same format |

167:### Static checks
168:
169:`make lint` runs three checks:
170:
171:- `ruff check`, including pydocstyle: every class, function and method in `app/`, `scripts/` and `migrations/` has a docstring.
172:- `ruff format --check`.
173:- `mypy --strict` over `app`, `scripts` and `migrations`, so every signature is annotated. `Any` appears explicitly in one place only: the JSON body read back from `idempotency_keys`.
174:
175:Tests are exempt from the docstring rule. Their shared fixtures and helpers, and the largest tests, have docstrings and annotations anyway. CI runs `make check` on every push.
176:
177:### Load
178:
179:`scripts/load.py` creates 1,100 firms of its own, with ids from 1000, and sends batches through the balancer. After the run it checks that no balance is negative, that the sum of balances is unchanged, that every load firm's balance matches its payments, and that no response was a 500. It exits non-zero if any check fails. Run `make reset` afterwards: the script deletes only its own firms (ids 1000 and up), and only before a run.
180:
181:```bash
182:make load ARGS="--scenario hot-payer --requests 2000 --concurrency 32"
183:make reset
184:```
185:
238:## Solution and approach
239:
240:### Data model
241:
242:The schema is created by Alembic migrations (`migrations/versions/0001_initial.py`), which the one-shot `migrate` service runs before any replica starts. The tables `firms` and `payments` have exactly the columns and types the task gives. I added only constraints:
243:
244:- a unique index on `firms.uuid`, because every request looks firms up by it under lock;
245:- foreign keys from `payments` to `firms`, because the task describes the columns as ids of `firms` rows.
246:
247:The third table, `idempotency_keys`, belongs to the idempotency extension described below. The service writes to it only when a request carries an `Idempotency-Key` header, so a request made exactly as the task describes touches only the two given tables.
248:
249:Before it starts serving, each replica compares the revision in the database's `alembic_version` table with the head revision of the migrations it ships with. If they differ, the replica refuses to start. A replica therefore never runs against a schema it was not built for: for example, when migrations failed, or when a newer image meets an older database.
250:
251:### The core: one transaction, ordered row locks
252:
253:Each request is one transaction at the default isolation level (Read Committed), so a batch is applied completely or not at all. Parsing, validation, conversion to cents, the per-payee sums and the request hash are all done before the transaction opens. Inside it there are only database statements:
254:
255:1. `SELECT set_config('lock_timeout', '5000ms', true)`.
256:2. Only when an `Idempotency-Key` was sent: claim the key (see below).
257:3. One query finds and locks every firm in the batch:
258:
259:   ```sql
260:   SELECT ... FROM firms WHERE uuid IN (...) ORDER BY id FOR NO KEY UPDATE
261:   ```
262:

118:   - The same key with a different body gives `422 idempotency_key_reuse`.
157:**Mutation check.** A concurrency test that stays green when the lock is removed proves nothing. So I broke the service three ways, one at a time, and ran the concurrency tests against each version:
204:| S3: stop one replica, then send the sample five times with one key | Five 201s, four of them replays. Balances changed once. |
286:Amounts are strings in the task and stay strings until they are converted to integer cents. The string must fully match `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?` (`fullmatch`, so `"1\n"` fails), be at most 11 characters and be greater than zero. The character class is `[0-9]`, not `\d`, because Python's `\d` also matches digits from other scripts. A JSON number such as `12.5` is rejected: it has already passed through floating point. `float` is not used anywhere.
340:The balancer accepts bodies up to 8 MB. The largest valid request is 1,000 payments with 500-character non-ASCII descriptions, about 1.1 MB, which is above nginx's 1 MB default.
344:The task sets no limit, but without one a single huge batch could hold locks on thousands of firms for seconds. The limit follows a criterion rather than taste: **the largest batch should hold its locks for at most about 5% of `lock_timeout`**, that is 250 ms of 5 s. That way about twenty maximal batches can queue on one firm before any of them times out.
354:In the project, through nginx, an uncontended 1,000-payment request takes 50 ms median and 70 ms at most, end to end. With four such batches from one payer in parallel, the median is 196 ms and the maximum 257.6 ms, about 7 ms over the budget. The difference is time spent queueing behind the other batches on the payer's row, not lock-hold time. I kept the limit at 1,000; both numbers are in the notes. A client with more than 1,000 payments splits them into several requests, and each request is atomic on its own. Both limits are configurable: `MAX_PAYMENTS_PER_REQUEST` and `MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH`.
378:- PostgreSQL 19 was released on 2026-11-19, a few days before this work. I stayed on 18: a major release a few days old is not where a payment service should start, and nothing here needs 19.
379:- Docker was not available where the design probes ran, so the stand was first verified during implementation (see above).
380:- My first draft of the mutation check was wrong. In the final check, removing `ORDER BY` (M2) is a mutation the tests do catch, through C3.
387:  - A JSON escape such as `"\ud800"` (a lone surrogate) in a description caused a 500. It is now a 422.
390:- **Stale balancer.** After the replicas were recreated, nginx still pointed at the old addresses and returned 504. `make up` now restarts it.
416:3. Keys are kept forever. Improvement: publish a retention period of at least 24 hours, so that client retries stay safe, and delete older keys by `created_at`.
432:I used **Claude Code** with three Claude models, chosen per step (`docs/agent-workflow.md`):
436:| Design and specification | Claude Fable 5.2 | `docs/spec.md`, with throwaway probes against PostgreSQL that confirmed the locking and idempotency behaviour |
437:| Implementation plan | Claude Fable 5.2 | `docs/plan.md`, nine tasks |
442:| Review after every task, and of every fix round | Mostly Opus 5.5; Sonnet 5.5 and once Haiku 5.5 for small re-reviews | Findings fixed until each task's review was clean |
443:| Whole-branch review | Claude Fable 5.2 | Three important findings, fixed in one wave |
453:When something was ambiguous, the controller did not stop. It made a ruling, wrote it down, and reported it. Every AI-written commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer that names its model.
455:**Logs.** `ai-logs/` holds every working session: the design sessions, the controller session with every subagent's transcript, and the review session. Two things differ from the raw export:
458:- Two aborted early attempts at starting the implementation are left out.
465:- storing only 201 responses;
469:Several started as the model's proposals that I accepted. These include `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, `JSON` instead of `JSONB`, storing only successful responses, the single error format with 422 for every rejection, and the key format. They are marked **[P]** in the spec.
471:During implementation the controller model made about twenty rulings on its own. The ones that changed the result:
474:- keeping the 1,000 limit after the contended run exceeded the budget;
477:- `make load` not resetting the database by itself.

486:                amount parsing), models.py, db.py, config.py, errors.py

## Findings, most important first

The README and the spec changed while I was reviewing: the README went from 488 to 511 lines, and there is uncommitted schema-revision work in progress. README line numbers below refer to the current 511-line file.

1. **Missing or misleading.** README:29–31, "`git clone https://github.com/yujinio/ta-firm-payments-challenge.git` … `make up`".
   - Source: `gh repo view` gives `defaultBranchRef: main`, and `git ls-tree --name-only origin/main` lists only `.gitignore` and `docs`. The code exists only on `feat/bulk-payment-service`, and no PR is open. From a clean clone there is no Makefile, so `make up` fails.
   - Fix: merge to `main` before sending the link, or use `git clone -b feat/bulk-payment-service …`.

2. **Wrong** for the repository as it stands. README:455, "`ai-logs/` holds every working session: the design sessions, the controller session …, and the review session".
   - Source: `find ai-logs` shows only `.gitkeep` (0 B). Task §3 and §7.2 require unedited logs.
   - plan.md:48 says "the independent review (Task 9, Step 1) is still to run". Step 5 (agent-workflow.md:35) is also missing from the table at README:434–444.
   - plan.md:564 requires the AI section to "list every session in `ai-logs/` with its tool and model". The README does not.
   - Fix: commit the logs, list them by session, and mention the review only once it exists.

3. **Missing.** README:498–511, the two questions: every box is unchecked. assignment.md:158 says "At the end of the README, also answer two quick questions." Fix: the author ticks one box in each, and adds the hours if more than 6h.

4. **Wrong.** README:469, "These include `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, `JSON` instead of `JSONB`, storing only successful responses … They are marked **[P]** in the spec."
   - spec.md:103 marks "Only the successful 201 response" as **[R]**, and README:465 also lists it under [R], so the README contradicts itself.
   - `grep '\[P\]'` finds no marker at spec.md:390 (`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`) or spec.md:255 (`JSON`/`JSONB`).
   - spec.md:11 defines [P] as "proposal … not yet confirmed separately", not "proposals that I accepted".
   - Fix: list only the real [P] items, the error format (spec.md:339) and the key format (spec.md:283), and use the spec's definition of [P].

5. **Wrong.** README:453, "Every AI-written commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer that names its model", read alongside README:436–437, which credit the spec and plan to Fable 5.2.
   - Source: commit fce9a5b ("docs: design spec, implementation plan and agent workflow") has `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`, and no commit names Fable.
   - Fix: say the trailer names the model of the session that made the commit, or correct the attribution.

6. **Wrong and Unsupported.** README:432, "three Claude models", and README:442, "Sonnet 5.5 and once Haiku 5.5 for small re-reviews".
   - The table itself names four models.
   - Haiku appears nowhere in agent-workflow.md or plan.md:90–97. The only reviewer model on record is the 4b re-reviewer, Sonnet (agent-workflow.md:34).
   - Fix: say "four models", and back the reviewer split with the logs or drop it.

7. **Unsupported.** Three counts have no source:
   - README:443, "Three important findings, fixed in one wave": plan.md:45 lists four fix-wave items (Content-Type message, host ports with loopback, body limit with Host, CI `stand`).
   - README:458, "Two aborted early attempts": agent-workflow.md:18 gives no count.
   - README:471, "about twenty rulings".
   - Fix: take the numbers from the logs once they are committed, or drop them.

8. **Wrong and Unsupported.** Who owns which decision contradicts itself:
   - "I kept the limit at 1,000" (README:354) against the controller ruling "keeping the 1,000 limit" (README:474).
   - "So I broke the service three ways" (README:157) against README:441, which says the mutation check was done by Opus subagents.
   - README:477, "`make load` not resetting the database by itself", is listed as a controller ruling. plan.md:46 calls the move of `make load` to host uv "the author's decision", and no document records a no-reset ruling.
   - Fix: give each decision one owner, consistent with the logs.

9. **Unsupported.** README:380, "My first draft of the mutation check was wrong. In the final check, removing `ORDER BY` (M2) is a mutation the tests do catch, through C3." It sits under "During design (found by throwaway probes…)".
   - git cannot show drafts that were never committed. In git, the spec's M2 row is unchanged since fce9a5b, and the first committed notes (`git show 95e72a0:docs/verification-notes.md`) already have C3 catching M2.
   - The only correction in git is to the cause, an unverified "LockRows over Seq Scan" fixed in 7c7f885. That happened during implementation.
   - The bullets at README:378–379 (PG 19, Docker unavailable) are not probe findings either.
   - Fix, if this is what was meant: "my first write-up gave an unverified cause for C2 staying clean under M2", moved under "During implementation".

10. **Misleading.** README:83, "To stop the stand, run `docker compose down`. To drop the data as well, run `docker compose down -v`."
    - Source: the compose file has no named volume. `docker inspect` on db-1 shows an anonymous `volume 2fa7c8fd… -> /var/lib/postgresql`.
    - Inferred, not tested, since restarts were off-limits: after `down`, the next `up` gets a fresh volume, so the firms are gone and `make seed` is needed. `-v` only removes the orphaned volume.
    - Fix: "`docker compose stop` keeps the data; after `down`, run `make up` and `make seed`". Or add a named volume.

11. **Missing or misleading: in flux.** README:128 says "151 tests passing", README:137 says "`tests/db` | 6", and README:249 states the replica schema-revision check as fact.
    - Source: `pytest --collect-only` now gives 156 tests, with db at 11, because of the untracked `tests/db/test_schema_revision.py`.
    - README:249 rests on the untracked `app/schema_revision.py` and an uncommitted change to `app/main.py`.
    - The layout at README:484–486 omits `schema_revision.py`.
    - CI evidence (run 45408968632, 151 passed) covers only 6abb684.
    - Fix: commit the work, then update the counts, the db row and the layout, and re-run CI.

12. **Wrong.** Test descriptions:
    - README:153, I5 "7 byte-identical replays": test_races.py:140 compares parsed dicts. Bytes are compared only in C7 (test_multiprocess.py:157). Fix: "identical (byte-identical over HTTP in C7)".
    - README:138, "I1–I9 cover idempotency" for `tests/api`: I5 is in `tests/concurrency/test_races.py`. Fix: "I1–I4, I6–I9".
    - README:145, C1 "three 201s, seven 422s": C1 runs in-process and counts `created`/`insufficient_funds` (test_races.py:54). HTTP status codes are checked only in C7 (test_multiprocess.py:138).

13. **Wrong (arithmetic).** README:340, "The largest valid request is 1,000 payments with 500-character non-ASCII descriptions, about 1.1 MB."
    - spec.md:151 says the same, but the figure holds only for 2-byte characters. A json.dumps of 1,000×500 characters is 1.60 MB with CJK, 2.10 MB with raw emoji, and 6.10 MB with `\u` escapes. The length check counts Python characters (service.py:87).
    - All of these still fit under 8 MB.
    - Fix: "1.1 to 6.1 MB depending on encoding".

14. **Misleading.** README:354 gives "the median is 196 ms", while README:193 gives p50 "193.2" for the same run.
    - Source: verification-notes.md:319–321 explains these as statistics.median and nearest-rank respectively.
    - Fix: use 193.2, or add that half-sentence from the notes.

15. **Unsupported.** No repository source backs these:
    - README:390, the stale balancer "returned 504": plan.md:43 records only the restart.
    - README:387, the lone surrogate "caused a 500": no document or commit says so.
    - README:416, "retention period of at least 24 hours": spec.md:656 says only "a time-to-live and periodic cleanup".
    - README:5, "`docs/verification-notes.md` records every measured and observed result quoted below": the probe figures (2,400/80, 109 ms, 40 threads) are in spec §5.7 and §17. Fix: "the notes and spec section 17".
    - README:286, "`float` is not used anywhere" (**Wrong**): main.py:55 has `duration_ms: float`. Fix: "never for money" (plan.md:18).

16. **Misleading.** README:22, "Podman with `docker-compose`".
    - The Makefile calls `docker compose`. The verified setup is a `docker` shim (`docker --version` → `podman version 5.8.2`), rootful (`podman machine inspect` → `true`), with Compose v5.1.3 as provider (spec.md:598).
    - README:424 meanwhile warns that legacy `docker-compose` v1 ignores `deploy.replicas`.
    - Fix: "Podman with a `docker` command (podman-docker) and Docker Compose v2+ as provider".

17. **Missing.** README:118, "The same key with a different body gives `422 idempotency_key_reuse`", and the S3 check at README:204 have no commands. spec.md:634 has reviewers run S3.
    - Fix: add `curl … -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-1' --data-binary @format-example-request.json`. I ran it and got 422 `idempotency_key_reuse`.
    - Also add the S3 steps: `docker stop $(docker compose ps -q app | head -1)`, five posts with one key, then `make up`.

## Verified correct
- Live: the sample returns 201 with the exact README body (ids 1–3, "13251.25"); balances are 3674875/170075/1405050; three repeats give 201, 201, 422 with the exact `insufficient_funds` JSON.
- Live: `curl -d` without a Content-Type gives 422 with the exact `Content-Type: application/json` message.
- Live: after `make reset`, format-example returns 201 and balances are 4849925/170075/230000. The arithmetic 10,246.25 is correct.
- Live: `demo-1` sent twice gives two 201s; `cmp` shows the bodies are byte-identical; the replay has `idempotent-replayed: true` from another upstream; the database has 3 payments and 1 key.
- Live: the S2 loop shows three X-Upstream lines (11/10/9).
- PDF (pypdf): the format example is on page 3 and the sample on page 4.
- At commit 6abb684, 151 tests = 64/6/63/18. CI run 45408968632: `151 passed`, ruff `All checks passed!`, mypy `no issues found`.
- The Make targets match the Makefile. LB_PORT and DB_PORT are honoured by compose, the Makefile and conftest. Ruff runs pydocstyle `D` and exempts tests (pyproject.toml). `Any` appears only in models.py:60.
- Error codes, statuses and messages, `Retry-After: 1`, 404/405/`http_error`, and details limited to loc/msg/type (main.py, errors.py, service.py).
- Transaction order is `set_config('lock_timeout','5000ms',true)`, then claim the key, then a single `IN (...) ORDER BY id` with `key_share=True` (FOR NO KEY UPDATE), then the checks, then insert, update and store (service.py:179–248).
- 55P03 and 40P01 map to busy, with an ERROR log for deadlock. Pool `TimeoutError` maps to busy (service.py:160–171).
- Amount rules: `[0-9]` fullmatch, at most 11 characters, greater than 0, at most INT32_MAX, StrictStr. U+0000 and lone surrogates are rejected (schemas.py).
- Key format 0x21–0x7E, 1–255 characters, first header wins; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; SHA-256 over cents; the column is JSON, not JSONB; only 201 responses are stored; keys are per payer.
- Pool 10, `max_overflow=0`, `pool_pre_ping`, `hide_parameters`; the AnyIO limit is set to the pool size; the engine is built once under a lock. The log record fields match main.py:96–106.
- Compose: postgres:18, a one-shot migrate, 3 replicas, nginx, ports on loopback, `client_max_body_size 8m`, a 2 s connect timeout, the X-Upstream header.
- Test mechanics: Barrier, pg_stat_activity polling, I-1/I-2 checked per round, C2 20×50, C3 200 batches on 16 threads with seed 20261121, C7 with `--workers 4`, the statement-order test.
- The M1–M3 table, M2 failing 3 of 3, and C2 staying clean under M2 (verification-notes.md:30–145).
- The load table, the machine and VM specs, 1,100 firms from id 1000, the load.py checks and exit code, and ~600/s (notes:217–310).
- 50.3/69.9 and 196/257.6 ms, the 250 ms budget, and the probe table 109/206/1,067 (spec §5.7, notes:314–343).
- S1–S3 on Podman 5.8.2 / Compose v5.1.3 with the 2 s delay. The CI jobs `check` and `stand` run on push and PR on ubuntu-latest.
- The spec §17 probe facts: SET LOCAL, JSONB reorder, pool error not a DBAPIError, U+0000, PG 19 on 2026-11-19, 2,400/80 on PG 16.
- Assumptions 1–11 match spec §4. Limitations 1–14 match spec §15 and §9.3, apart from finding 15.
- The [R] list (README:462–467) matches spec §5.1–5.7.
- Steps 1a, 2 and 3–4 and the model split match agent-workflow.md:29–36. The Sonnet trailers are on tasks 1–2 and the Opus trailers on 3–8. The subagent-driven flow and the ruling procedure match agent-workflow.md:17–19.
- Task §7.3: solution, issues, assumptions, improvements, and run/verify are all present.

## Method
- On your instruction I did not run `make check`, `make test` or pytest; the counts come from `pytest --collect-only` and CI.
- I skipped `make load` because `scripts/load.py` was being edited; I checked its figures against the notes instead.
- After the live checks I ran `make reset`. The database is back at 5000000/50000/200000 with 0 payments and 0 keys.
